comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
I don't agree with this, just like I don't agree with "consent" in the area of sex/rape. Both cases are excellent examples of how our codependence has been normalized.

Consent necessarily implies the pre-existing will on someone's part to do what we, in response, either consent to allow or refuse to allow.

Why the fuck would we approach either government or sex/rape this way? Why the fuck would we just gloss over the questions of what motivates the will we've been accosted by, whether it's OK for them to be so motivated, whether that will intends on good or evil, and whether it should have been allowed to form at all (as opposed to be allowed to act) -- as if there were no questions at all about it?

Well, the answer to all of that is: our codependence.

This is why I insist that "consent" is a Trojan Horse. The real test should be permission.

WE NEED TO ASK FOR PERMISSION BEFORE WE FORM THE WILL TO MAKE DECISIONS AND TAKE ACTIONS THAT DIRECTLY AFFECT OTHERS.

THAT is what true lovers do. THAT is what true mentors, guides, and experts do.

"Consent" is pigshit.

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
All of you who are certain that governments, laws, authorities, and other coercive, violence-based staples of "civilization" are necessary to prevent "chaos from ensuing" and are mandatory to secure collective safety:

Read my conversation about it with DeepSeek.

https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/60b3f575-5ff8-4714-8a88-22aa1183c168

READ and THINK and show me HOW SPECIFICALLY we didn't cover ALL the major objections to the idea.

READ and THINK and show me HOW SPECIFICALLY any of those objections turn out to be even so much as slightly more than superstitions.

In my early forays into AI chatbot conversations, I asked them to describe how a society that has no laws, authorities, governments would work. This was to see how well they could reason and how biased they were.

They all provided very similar (almost spookily similar) responses to the effect that, ultimately, the idea was utopian, idealistic, impractical and, at best, feasible only on very small scales.

So, I argued with them. I sent one of them into a spin it never returned from. I pointed out so many bogus claims and self-contradictions to another one (I think Copilot) that it shut the conversation down: "Let's talk about something else." 😆

So, I thought I'd test DeepSeek similarly.

It did pretty well. Not as biased out of the gate, brought up some good points. Parroted the same old "challenges" I've heard for decades, but when I explained how they're bogus, it recognized my points and agreed.

You law-and-order cultists: see if you can do better.

https://chat.deepseek.com/a/chat/s/60b3f575-5ff8-4714-8a88-22aa1183c168

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
So, another contribution to my efforts to expose the chocked-full-of-shit insanity of this thing we call "ownership".

Just a little math exercise -- not so much to prove the point that ownership is a mental illness, but just to get you clear on what I'm talking about as I demonstrate exactly why it's a mental illness.

Consider the fact that an item of property has been deprived by the owner from 8.2 billion others (minus the owner).

Just take in, as best you can, the unimaginable scope of the ever-present deprivation occurring every fucking second of every fucking day for every single human being on Earth. Even the "rich" are deprived just like everyone else -- deprived of everything they do not own -- which lack is exactly what turns them into obsessive, deranged, hoarding fiends.

Nobody grasps numbers in the sextillions. Nobody grasps numbers in the quintillions. Nobody grasps numbers in even the quadrillions. We kind of have a feeble grasp of millions and billions and trillions -- barely. No one has actually seen them. We've seen thousands, though.

Realize how profoundly evil this deprivation on scales we can't even imagine is. Real deprivation of real necessities and desirables from every single person on the planet, all the time. For the sake of what?

For the sake of "security" from absolutely paranoid, hysterical fantasies that everyone wants what we have and anybody, potentially everybody, could take it away from us without notice or a clue.

Fucking bizarre levels of insane, phobic narcissism, in other words.

No. Virtually no one is dying to be you. Almost no one is dying to take what you have. Almost no one even knows you're there -- and most of them don't really care about you one way or the other.

You are not all that, not to anyone. Only in your sick, delusional, fever dreams.

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
To everyone who ever supported or defended the practice of ownership, here are some indisputable facts:

Every society known to us that was not dubbed "primitive", "barabaric", "wild", or "savage" organized itself around the promotion and protection of ownership.

Many "primitive", "barabaric", "wild", or "savage" societies, likewise, organized themselves around the promotion and protection of ownership.

"Ownership" in these societies boiled down to the legally recognized right of one person or party to preemptively, unilaterally deprive a necessity or desirable from all the rest of humankind.

I want you to think about that for a minute.

Think about the "preemptively deprive" part and what its implications are.

People mock the idea of a single person or party standing against the rest of humankind to say they're wrong while, at the same time, when it comes to depriving humankind of real necessities and desirables, it’s, "Oh, well! That's different! That's all the rage, and more power to it!"

🤯 🤦🙇‍♂️

And then think of the magnitude involved in establishing, legitimizing, and protecting this right to deprive all humankind of a necessity or desirable without any regard to fact. (More about that in the next note.)

No wonder laws and violent punishment must be brought to bear to protect such insanity, because otherwise no one in their right mind would allow it.

What do I mean by "without any regard to fact"? How does ownership disregard fact?

I mean that without even wondering, let alone questioning, let alone ascertaining, whether deprivation is in fact either necessary or advisable with regards to the real people who in fact actually could take or use or destroy resources or property, ownership preemptively, in principle, unilaterally deprives all others, period, case closed without a hearing, let alone a trial. Whether it's a good idea or not, whether it's beneficial or destructive, or whether it's even relevant or not, ownership is single-minded in its obsession that THERE WILL INDEED BE DEPRIVATION.

I'd argue: psychotically obsessive.

Now, ask yourself: does ownership more closely fit the model of sharing, friendship, peerness, care, and love? Or does it fit the model of predation, adversariality, paranoia, self-interest, and violence?

Then, answer the fucking question.

This is such a good example of the power of honesty.

We don't need to "prove" anything. We just need to be honest, report honestly what we experience and witness, share our honest perspectives on it, our honest opinions about what it means it, and ask honest questions about it.

If the reaction we get is to trample our honest pearls underfoot and turn to tear us to pieces, then we know we're dealing with pigs in the sense of Jesus' metaphor.

Honest people don't do that to honest people.

This mother's approach to the problem is genius:

https://www.facebook.com/share/r/14yeWqMuYp/
